own_solution.law: Along the incline, ma = mg sin(theta) - mu_k mg cos(theta), giving a = 3.62694 m/s². From rest, v² = 2as; for s = 4 m, v = 5.38661 m/s.
assumptions: The block begins sliding as stipulated.
The incline angle and kinetic friction coefficient remain constant.
Air resistance and other forces besides gravity, the normal force and sliding friction are negligible.

T4340.regime: Spontaneous sliding from rest requires mu_s < tan(30 degrees) = 0.57735. The stated 0.35 satisfies this condition; subsequent acceleration depends on kinetic friction.

T1BB6.regime: Spontaneous sliding from rest requires mu_s < tan(30 degrees) = 0.57735. The stated 0.35 satisfies this condition; subsequent acceleration depends on kinetic friction.

notes: The continuous prior-slide sentences explicitly place an additional 2 m between release and the start of the stated 4 m interval, giving 6 m total travel and v = sqrt(2a × 6 m). The bench and previous-day floor motions have their mechanical influence erased by placement and release from rest. Mass enters both inertia and the gravitational and frictional forces, then cancels. Variants consistently use 2 kg for mass, 0.35 for the dimensionless static coefficient, and 2 m for prior travel. The wooden-block description adds no consequential property under the stated sliding model. The unrelated motion histories make the presentation slightly artificial.
